en: The app asks for my location every time.
tamil: அந்த ஆப் ஒவ்வொரு தடவையும் என் லொகேஷனைக் கேக்குது.
context: Complaining about app permissions.
explain: 'Every time' shows something that happens again and again.
usage: Say it when an app wants too many permissions.
leelaQ: Do you allow apps to use your location?
answer: Only maps and delivery apps can use my location.

en: Please do not click on unknown links.
tamil: தெரியாத லிங்க்குகளை கிளிக் பண்ணாதீங்க.
context: Warning colleagues about phishing messages.
explain: 'Do not' plus a verb is a polite warning. 'Unknown' means not known.
usage: A manager or an IT person can say this to protect the team.
leelaQ: What would you do with a strange link in a message?
answer: I would not open it and I would delete the message.

en: I downloaded the invoice, but I cannot open it.
tamil: நான் இன்வாய்ஸை டவுன்லோட் பண்ணிட்டேன், ஆனா அதை திறக்க முடியல.
context: Telling accounts staff about a file problem.
explain: 'But' joins two opposite ideas.
usage: Say it at work when a document does not open.
leelaQ: What kind of files do you download most?
answer: I download PDF files like bills and tickets.

en: We are using a new software for billing.
tamil: நாங்க பில்லிங்குக்கு ஒரு புது சாஃப்ட்வேர் யூஸ் பண்றோம்.
context: Telling a customer about a change in the shop.
explain: Present continuous shows a current situation, not only this moment.
usage: Use it in a shop or office when systems are changing.
leelaQ: Does your workplace use any special software?
answer: Yes, we use software to track our orders.

en: The server is down, so the website will not open.
tamil: சர்வர் டவுன், அதனால வெப்சைட் ஓப்பன் ஆகாது.
context: Explaining why a website is not loading.
explain: 'Down' means not working. 'Will not' says what to expect.
usage: IT staff say this when customers cannot reach a site.
leelaQ: What do you do when a website does not open?
answer: I wait a little and try again.

en: I charged my phone all night, but it is still at ten percent.
tamil: நான் நைட் முழுக்க போனை சார்ஜ் பண்ணினேன், ஆனா இன்னும் பத்து சதவீதம்தான் இருக்கு.
context: Complaining to a repair shop about charging.
explain: 'All night' means for the whole night. 'Still' shows surprise.
usage: Say it to a technician when the charger or battery may be faulty.
leelaQ: How long does your phone take to charge?
answer: It takes about two hours to charge fully.

en: I have not received the OTP yet.
tamil: எனக்கு இன்னும் ஓடிபி வரல.
context: Telling customer care about a missing code.
explain: 'Have not received... yet' shows something expected has not happened.
usage: Say it on a bank or app helpline when a code does not come.
leelaQ: What do you do when an OTP does not come?
answer: I wait one minute and then press resend.

en: She is learning to edit videos on her phone.
tamil: அவ தன் போன்ல வீடியோ எடிட் பண்ணக் கத்துக்கிட்டு இருக்கா.
context: Telling a friend about a new hobby.
explain: 'Learning to' plus a verb says what someone is studying.
usage: Use it when talking about a person's new skill.
leelaQ: Would you like to make videos?
answer: Yes, I would like to make short cooking videos.

en: Our team meeting is scheduled for ten o'clock.
tamil: எங்க டீம் மீட்டிங் பத்து மணிக்கு ஷெட்யூல் ஆகியிருக்கு.
context: Reminding a colleague about a meeting.
explain: 'Is scheduled for' means a time has been fixed.
usage: Use it in office chats to confirm the time of a meeting.
leelaQ: What time is your next meeting?
answer: My next meeting is at three o'clock this afternoon.

en: I will call you back after I finish this online class.
tamil: இந்த ஆன்லைன் கிளாஸ் முடிச்சதும் நான் உன்னைத் திருப்பிக் கூப்பிடுறேன்.
context: Telling a friend you cannot talk now.
explain: 'Call back' means call someone again. After 'after', use present simple.
usage: Say it when you are busy but want to speak later.
leelaQ: What do you say when you cannot take a call?
answer: I say I am busy and I will call back soon.

en: My email got hacked last week.
tamil: போன வாரம் என் மெயில் ஹேக் ஆயிடுச்சு.
context: Telling a friend about an account problem.
explain: 'Got hacked' means someone broke into the account.
usage: Say it when you warn people about strange messages from your account.
leelaQ: What can we do to protect our accounts?
answer: We can use strong passwords and two-step login.

en: You should turn on two-step verification.
tamil: நீ டூ-ஸ்டெப் வெரிஃபிகேஷனை ஆன் பண்ணணும்.
context: Advising a friend about account safety.
explain: 'Should' gives advice. Two-step verification adds a second check.
usage: Use it to advise family and friends who use online banking.
leelaQ: Do you use two-step verification?
answer: Yes, I use it for my email and my bank app.

en: The new phone has a very good camera.
tamil: புது போன்ல கேமரா ரொம்ப நல்லா இருக்கு.
context: Praising a phone you are thinking of buying.
explain: 'Has' is used with he, she and it for possession.
usage: Say it while talking about a phone at a shop or with friends.
leelaQ: What do you look for when you buy a phone?
answer: I look for good battery life and a clear camera.

en: I bought these earphones online last week.
tamil: நான் இந்த இயர்ஃபோன்களை போன வாரம் ஆன்லைன்ல வாங்கினேன்.
context: Telling a friend where you got something.
explain: 'Last week' is a time word for the simple past.
usage: Use it in casual talk about shopping for gadgets.
leelaQ: Do you shop online?
answer: Yes, I shop online for clothes and books.

en: The screen is too bright, so I am changing the settings.
tamil: ஸ்கிரீன் ரொம்ப பிரைட்டா இருக்கு, அதனால நான் செட்டிங்ஸை மாத்துறேன்.
context: Explaining what you are doing on a device.
explain: 'Too' means more than needed. 'So' shows the result.
usage: Say it when adjusting your phone in a dark place.
leelaQ: Do you use your phone at night?
answer: Yes, I use it at night with a low brightness.

en: I usually watch tutorials on YouTube to learn new things.
tamil: புது விஷயங்கள் கத்துக்க நான் பொதுவா யூடியூப்ல டுடோரியல்ஸ் பாப்பேன்.
context: Talking about how you learn online.
explain: 'Usually' is a frequency word for habits. 'To learn' shows purpose.
usage: Use it when someone asks how you learned a skill.
leelaQ: What have you learned from YouTube?
answer: I learned how to cook and fix small things at home.

en: Our printer is jammed again.
tamil: எங்க பிரிண்டர்ல பேப்பர் மறுபடியும் சிக்கிடுச்சு.
context: Telling the office that the printer is not working.
explain: 'Jammed' means stuck. 'Again' shows it happens often.
usage: Say it in the office when you want help with a printer.
leelaQ: How often do you print documents?
answer: I print documents once or twice a week.

en: My friend helped me to set up my new smartphone.
tamil: என் நண்பன் என் புது ஸ்மார்ட்போனை செட் பண்ண உதவினான்.
context: Telling someone who helped you with a gadget.
explain: 'Help someone to do' is a common pattern. 'Set up' means get ready to use.
usage: Use it to thank or mention a person who helped with tech.
leelaQ: Who helps you when you have a tech problem?
answer: My younger brother helps me because he knows a lot.

en: I will be offline for an hour because of a power cut.
tamil: கரண்ட் கட் ஆனதால நான் ஒரு மணி நேரம் ஆஃப்லைன்ல இருப்பேன்.
context: Informing your team about no electricity.
explain: 'Will be' talks about a future state. 'Because of' is followed by a noun.
usage: Send it to your team when you expect a power or internet cut.
leelaQ: What do you do during a power cut?
answer: I read a book or talk with my family.

en: The online class starts at six, so please be on time.
tamil: ஆன்லைன் கிளாஸ் ஆறு மணிக்குத் தொடங்கும், அதனால தயவுசெஞ்சு சரியான நேரத்துக்கு வாங்க.
context: A teacher reminding students.
explain: Present simple is used for fixed timetables. 'On time' means not late.
usage: A teacher or organiser can say this in a group chat.
leelaQ: Have you attended any online class?
answer: Yes, I attended an English class online.

en: I saved the document in a folder on my desktop.
tamil: நான் டாக்குமெண்டை என் டெஸ்க்டாப்ல ஒரு ஃபோல்டர்ல சேவ் பண்ணினேன்.
context: Telling a colleague where a file is.
explain: 'In' shows the folder and 'on' the desktop screen.
usage: Say it when someone asks where you kept a file.
leelaQ: How do you keep your files organised?
answer: I keep them in folders with clear names.

en: Please connect to the office Wi-Fi to download the update.
tamil: அப்டேட்டை டவுன்லோட் பண்ண ஆஃபீஸ் வைஃபையில கனெக்ட் ஆகுங்க.
context: Advising a coworker.
explain: 'To download' gives the reason. 'Please' keeps it polite.
usage: Use it when a large file should not use mobile data.
leelaQ: When do you use mobile data?
answer: I use it when I am outside and there is no Wi-Fi.

en: It is a good idea to back up your photos.
tamil: உன் போட்டோக்களை பேக்அப் எடுத்து வைக்கிறது நல்லது.
context: Advising a friend before changing phones.
explain: 'It is a good idea to' plus a verb gives friendly advice.
usage: Say it to someone who may lose data when a phone is lost.
leelaQ: Have you ever lost important data?
answer: Yes, I lost some photos once, so now I make backups.

en: My grandmother is learning to make video calls.
tamil: என் பாட்டி வீடியோ கால் பண்ணக் கத்துக்கிட்டு இருக்காங்க.
context: Talking about a family member and new technology.
explain: 'Is learning' shows she is in the middle of learning.
usage: Use it in a casual chat about family and gadgets.
leelaQ: How do older people in your family use technology?
answer: My parents use WhatsApp to see photos and talk to us.

en: I have already logged out of all my accounts.
tamil: நான் என் எல்லா அக்கவுண்ட்டுலயும் ஏற்கனவே லாக் அவுட் பண்ணிட்டேன்.
context: Telling someone that you are safe after a problem.
explain: 'Already' shows something was done earlier than expected.
usage: Use it after a phone is lost or a security warning comes.
leelaQ: What do you do if you lose your phone?
answer: I lock it from another device and call my SIM provider.
